6. Approximation

Approximating continuous functions by polynomials and taming families of functions — the core approximation theorems.

  • Arzelà–Ascoli Theorem — When does a family of continuous functions hide a uniformly convergent subsequence? Uniform boundedness plus equicontinuity lets the diagonal argument extract one. Contrast with xnx^nxn, where it fails.
  • Weierstrass Approximation Theorem — Every continuous function on [0,1][0,1][0,1] is uniformly approximable by polynomials — watch the Bernstein polynomials Bn(f)B_n(f)Bn​(f) close in on fff as nnn grows. The fine estimates of the convergence proof are sketched at the idea level.
  • Stone–Weierstrass Theorem — A subalgebra that separates points and contains the constants is uniformly dense — trigonometric polynomials on the circle close in on the triangle wave ∣x∣|x|∣x∣, with no algebraic polynomial in sight.
  • Müntz–Szász Theorem — Approximate x\sqrt{x}x​ by least squares and watch the theorem decide: the dense basis {1,x,…,xN}\{1, x, \ldots, x^N\}{1,x,…,xN} (λn=n\lambda_n = nλn​=n, ∑1n=∞\sum \frac{1}{n} = \infty∑n1​=∞) shrinks its error 0.1003→0.0708→0.05440.1003 \to 0.0708 \to 0.05440.1003→0.0708→0.0544, while the sparse basis {1,x,x4,…,xN2}\{1, x, x^4, \ldots, x^{N^2}\}{1,x,x4,…,xN2} (∑1n2=π26<∞\sum \frac{1}{n^2} = \frac{\pi^2}{6} < \infty∑n21​=6π2​<∞) stays stuck near 0.160.160.16.
